page7_img_1.png.title: Apache SVN commit r291558 log entry (no bug ID)
page7_img_1.png.description: A plain-text SVN commit log showing revision r291558 by user “pquerna” on 2005-09-26 with a two-line message. The entry lists the changed path (M /httpd/httpd/trunk/Makefile.in) and the brief comment: “As recommended by nd, build docs for all languages.” There is no BugZilla ID or other bug-tracker reference in the message — the paper uses this commit as an example of a fix tied to a mailing-list discussion where the commit text gives almost no evidence it is a bug-fix, so automated linking heuristics would likely miss it.

page8_img_1.png.title: Anonymized developers: linked vs not-linked commit counts
page8_img_1.png.description: A two-column anonymized table listing developer identifiers (single letters) with, for each, the number of commits that were manually annotated as “Linked” to a bug report and the number annotated as “Not Linked.” The left and right halves of the table show names a, c, e, g, i, k, m, o, q and b, d, f, h, j, l, n, p respectively; examples include a: 0 linked / 6 not linked, b: 10 / 5, d: 11 / 8, and q: 4 / 0. The row totals at the bottom report 26 linked commits versus 52 not-linked commits overall. This table underpins the paper’s finding that linking behavior varies substantially across individual developers (reported statistical significance p = 0.002).

page3_img_1.png.title: Comparison of Apache original dataset and six-week evaluation sample
page3_img_1.png.description: Two-column table comparing the full Apache dataset (2004-06-18 to 2008-04-25) against the six-week evaluation sample (2005-09-23 to 2005-11-18). The full dataset contains 2,409 bug reports (559 fixed = 23.20%, 256 linked = 10.63%, 364 duplicates = 15.11%, 766 invalid = 31.80%) and 8,580 commit messages (472 linked = 5.50%, 0 empty), with 1,827 distinct bug reporters and 63 developers. The evaluation sample has 103 bug reports (23 fixed = 22.33%, 10 linked = 9.71%, 8 duplicates = 7.77%, 38 invalid = 36.89%) and 493 commit messages (29 linked = 5.88%, 0 empty), with 98 distinct reporters and 23 developers. Overall the linked-bug and linked-commit proportions in the sample (≈9.7% and ≈5.9%) are similar to the original dataset (≈10.6% and ≈5.5%), while duplicate and invalid-report proportions differ (sample shows fewer duplicates but a higher invalid rate).

page9_img_1.png.title: Commit-feature boxplots: linked vs unlinked bug-fix commits
page9_img_1.png.description: Four side-by-side boxplots contrast commits that were linked to bug reports ("Linked") with those that were not ("Not Linked") across four measures: weighted experience of the original revision authors (y-axis labeled as commit count), number of files changed, experience of the fixing author (commit count), and proportion file-ownership of the fixing author. Visually, linked commits show a modestly higher median weighted-experience (with large high-end outliers above ~1500 commits), tend to touch more than a single file while unlinked fixes are largely single-file, and are associated with more experienced fix authors (higher median); conversely, unlinked commits have higher median file-ownership proportions, consistent with the paper’s “anti-social” ownership hypothesis. The authors caution these are exploratory, visually suggestive patterns from a small sample and are not reported as statistically conclusive in the paper.

page4_img_1.png.title: Linkster screenshot showing integrated commit, bug, and blame/diff views
page4_img_1.png.description: The image is a composite screenshot of Linkster with three synchronized panes: (a) a Commit Information pane (top-left) listing revisions with author, date and one-line messages (example rows by author “jorton”), the full commit message area, a file list (double-clickable to view diffs), annotation checkboxes (e.g., “Bug Fix”) and a Bug IDs box pre-populated with 35330 and a free-text notes field reading “Backport of bug fix from trunk into 2.2.x branch.” (b) a Bug Information pane (right) showing a scrollable bug list (including entry 35330), tabs for Extended Bug Entry/Bug Activity/Fixing Files and bug attributes such as Status=RESOLVED, Severity=regression, Priority=P2, Product=Apache httpd-2, Version=2.1.7, Resolution=FIXED, plus the chronological bug comments. (c) a Blame & Diff pane (bottom) labeled “Blame Diff for Commit 97380” with a left pre-commit view (removed lines highlighted red and prefixed ‘−’), a right post-commit view (added lines in green with ‘+’), and a thumbnail/scroll bar overview; numbered callouts (1–15) identify these UI elements and the screenshot illustrates Linkster’s drag‑and‑drop linking, double‑click to view diffs, and line-level blame navigation used during the authors’ manual annotations.
